title: The Taster
logline: A tea taster tells a whole estate's story through sight, smell, taste and touch, then gives it a grade: a name built entirely from the senses.
human_question: How much of what we 'know' about a thing is just what came in through our senses, gathered under a name?

premise.story: A day of tasting and grading, and the decisions and livelihoods that depend on it.
premise.place: A hill-country tea factory and its tasting room.
premise.experience: Mist, leaf, the loud slurp of tasting, an attention so sharp it becomes almost visible.

concept_links.why: The sense bases and elements: seeing, smelling, tasting, touching as the doors through which a 'thing' is known.
Grades and names assembled from sense qualities.

what_camera_could_observe: Rows of cups; the taster's ritual
what_must_be_real: The actual tasting practice and its consequences for workers and sales.

possible_arc.turn: At the table, the leaf becomes a set of sensations, then a name.
possible_arc.ending_open: The grade and what follows from it.

requirements: A working factory with a tasting practice
Permission from management and consent from workers

suggestions.name: Tea country near Hunnasgiriya / the Knuckles foothills
suggestions.why: Continuity: the same hill road Chathura travels in Ep 1 and Ep 100.
suggestions.verify: Identify an active factory with tasting on site.

suggestions.name: Uva highlands (Haputale / Bandarawela)
suggestions.verify: Access, permissions and current conditions are unverified.

risks: Estate labour conditions: must be honest, not decorative
drop_if: Tasting happens only in a city office with no link to the estate

connections.note: Both show a map of experience learned through practice.

unknowns: No participant, access or event has been found or confirmed. Everything above is a research direction.
